clue.text: Layer pastry in turnover included in amount

indicators.note: being included in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a sum is an amount or total

indicators.note: a turnover flips something over, so the word for pastry is read backwards

parts.note: a tart is a pastry case with a filling

explanation.surface: A baker's instruction about layering pastry inside a turnover, with quantities measured out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' looks like the pastry dish, but 'in turnover' signals reversal, and 'included in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratum is a geological or social layer, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cocktail, as mixed with cider

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are shaken up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cocktail made by mixing with cider.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidecar is a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice.

clue.text: Someone engaged in boating commotion on East River

parts.note: a row is a noisy commotion
R is the abbreviation for River on maps

explanation.surface: A boater caught up in a commotion on a river in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: A rower propels a boat with oars, so is someone boating.

clue.text: Trunk and spreading roots

indicators.note: spreading roots move apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree's trunk with its roots spreading out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' and 'roots' suggest a tree; the definition is the human trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the human body's trunk, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Male representative before a battle

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before the last

parts.note: an agent acts as a representative

explanation.surface: A male delegate turns up just before a battle begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A battle' looks like the definition, but the A belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta was the 1859 battle in northern Italy where France and Sardinia beat Austria.

clue.text: A Slav describing British trick cyclist?

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one word goes around another

parts.note: a Croat is a Slav from Croatia

explanation.surface: A Slavic man is described as a British psychiatrist, 'trick cyclist' being slang for one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trick cyclist' is British slang for a psychiatrist; here it is taken literally, a performer doing stunts on a bike, hence the question mark. 'Describing' means drawing around: CROAT goes around B.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer doing stunts on a bicycle is one kind of gymnastic entertainer, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Object of performing recital

indicators.note: letters that perform are put through their paces, so rearranged

explanation.surface: The purpose of performing a recital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' reads as 'purpose' but means a thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is an item or thing, a sense shared with object.

clue.text: English method appearing in list as a good example to follow

indicators.note: pieces appearing in a word sit inside it

parts.note: a roll is a list of names
a mode is a manner or method

explanation.surface: An English method listed as an exemplary approach.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is a person whose behaviour others imitate.

clue.text: Thrilling ride, first in Blackpool — one going on gripped tightly

indicators.note: one piece goes on after the previous
the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: tight means drunk, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rider on a Blackpool roller coaster grips the bar tightly.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackpool is an English seaside resort with a famous fairground. 'Tightly' signals rearrangement of GRIPPED into GDIPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: A big dipper is a British name for a roller coaster, a fairground thrill ride.

clue.text: Anxiety of soldiers caught in wrongful act

indicators.note: something caught in another is held inside it

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: Troops worried about being caught in a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Torment is severe mental suffering, a stronger kind of distress.

clue.text: Utterly depressed? True

parts.note: feeling down means feeling depressed
right means correct or true

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person is utterly depressed, and the reply confirms it is true.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright as an adverb means thoroughly or completely, as in 'downright rude'.

clue.text: An effervescent beer in village restaurant

indicators.note: the answer sits in the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: A fizzy beer served in a village restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light, bottom-fermented, sparkling beer.

clue.text: Satirical drawing showing face of Onassis on board container

indicators.note: something on board is inside a vessel, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a carton is a cardboard container

indicators.note: the face of something is its front, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: A satirical cartoon shows the shipping magnate Onassis on board a container ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' evokes Onassis's shipping fleet, but it is the container signal: the face letter boards the box.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartoon is a humorous or satirical drawing, the kind printed in newspapers.

clue.text: Join together to thoroughly search home, last in terrace

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
in means at home

indicators.note: the last letter of the word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: People join together to search a house thoroughly, finishing with the last one in the terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: A terrace is a British row of joined houses.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine things is to unite or merge them into one.

clue.text: Scoundrel in favour of cutting repayment

indicators.note: a piece that cuts into another is placed within it

parts.note: a rebate is a partial repayment of money
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A rogue supports cutting back on repayments.
explanation.definitionFit: A reprobate is an unprincipled person, a rogue or rascal.

clue.text: Agent set up one-time entertainer

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means read upwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
one-time means former or previous

explanation.surface: A talent agent sets up a former entertainer.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer is an actor, singer or other entertainer.

clue.text: Accused over an assault

parts.note: on means about, over a matter
a is the indefinite article, like an
a charge is a military assault

explanation.surface: Someone accused of an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held on a charge has been formally accused of a crime.

clue.text: Drank to excess back in warehouse

indicators.note: back says the word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to tope is to drink alcohol to excess, so toped is the past tense

explanation.surface: Someone drank too much back in the warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storage building, a synonym of storehouse.

clue.text: Operatic heroine, not quite conventional

indicators.note: not quite the whole word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: normal means conventional or standard

explanation.surface: An opera heroine is described as not quite ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is the title heroine of Bellini's opera, a Druid priestess.

clue.text: Bishop imprisoned by peers — dopes!

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held within the word

parts.note: nobles are peers of the realm
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop locked up by fellow peers, who are called idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dopes' reads as idiots but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To nobble a racehorse is to drug it, so it is a verb synonym for drugs.

clue.text: Place that may suit one in Mayfair?

definitions.text: Place that may suit one in Mayfair?

parts.words: Place that may suit one in Mayfair?
parts.note: the London street famous for bespoke tailoring lies in Mayfair, where one may be fitted with a suit; 'suit' reads as both 'please' and 'clothe'

explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is an upmarket district of central London; its famous tailoring street makes men's suits.
explanation.definitionFit: The street is London's home of bespoke tailoring, the place where gentlemen are fitted for suits.

clue.text: Medieval warrior from small tribe featured in article

indicators.note: featured in a word means appearing inside it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a race is a people or tribe

explanation.surface: A newspaper article features a medieval fighter from a small tribe.
explanation.definitionFit: Saracens were Muslim warriors fought by the Crusaders.

clue.text: Cover Montana? Not all of that state

indicators.note: Not all of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to blanket Montana, but not the whole of that state.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermont is a US state in New England, so it fits 'that state'.

clue.text: We back Lone Ranger film?

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Fans support a Lone Ranger movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lone Ranger is a cowboy hero, so a film about him is an example of a cowboy genre film.

clue.text: Trade unionist perhaps runs into trouble

indicators.note: one piece goes into the other

parts.note: bother means trouble or fuss
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A trade unionist runs into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Union members traditionally address each other as fellow kin, so a trade unionist is an example of this comrade.

clue.text: Dodges in game

definitions.meaning: dodges are scams or swindles, dishonest schemes
a fast court game played with a hard ball, ancestor of squash

explanation.definitionFit: Rackets are both fraudulent schemes and a racquet sport played against walls.

clue.text: Copper with cast, undemanding

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to shy is to throw or cast

explanation.surface: A policeman in a plaster cast gets an easy job.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job is easy and comfortable, requiring little effort.

clue.text: Live way out, across sierra

indicators.note: one piece goes across another, enclosing it

parts.note: an exit is a way out
Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Living far out, across a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sierra' suggests mountains but is the radio code word for S.
explanation.definitionFit: To exist is to be alive, to have being.

clue.text: Rule changed to accommodate married primate

indicators.note: accommodating something means housing it inside
changed says the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rule is altered so a married primate can be housed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changed' rearranges RULE into LEUR; 'to accommodate' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemurs are Madagascan primates with long tails.

clue.text: Lively exchange of opinions might make one angry before launch

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: cross means angry
to fire a rocket is to launch it

explanation.surface: A heated argument might make someone angry before blasting off.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossfire is figuratively a heated back-and-forth of remarks or argument.

clue.text: Singular desire before appearing live as one working in theatre

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before the last one

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
an urge is a desire
a show that is live is on

explanation.surface: An actor's singular wish to go on before appearing live in the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' means the operating theatre, not the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon works in an operating theatre, so this is a cryptic description of a doctor.

clue.text: Attempt to deceive, positioning moon round far side of Mercury

indicators.note: round means placed around another piece

parts.note: Triton is the largest moon of Neptune

indicators.note: the far side is the last letter

explanation.surface: An astronomical deception: moving a moon round the far side of Mercury.
explanation.walkthrough: Triton is Neptune's chief moon; Y, the last letter of Mercury, goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: To try something on is to attempt a bluff or a deception to see if it works.
